title: Add customer
definition: Create the personal record and customer record for a new customer.

parameters.name: PersonID
parameters.description: Unused identifier for the new PERSON row.

parameters.name: ZipCode
parameters.description: Postal code, stored as text to preserve leading zeros.

statements.sql:
INSERT INTO PERSON (PersonID, LastName, FirstName, Address, City, State, ZipCode, Telephone)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?);

INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (PersonID, CustomerID, EmailAddress, CreditCardNumber, Rating)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?);

SELECT P.PersonID, P.LastName, P.FirstName, P.Address, P.City, P.State, P.ZipCode, P.Telephone,
       C.CustomerID, C.EmailAddress, C.Rating
FROM PERSON P JOIN CUSTOMER C ON C.PersonID = P.PersonID
WHERE C.CustomerID = ?
ORDER BY C.CustomerID;

notes: Both inserts belong to one transaction. If either insert fails, roll back both. The same PersonID is bound to both inserts. This creates a customer profile; account enrollment is a separate operation. The SELECT verifies the resulting row before the test rollback.

title: Edit customer contact information
definition: Update the telephone number and email address of the same existing customer.

parameters.name: CustomerID
parameters.description: Identifier of the one customer being edited.

statements.sql:
UPDATE PERSON P
JOIN CUSTOMER C ON C.PersonID = P.PersonID
SET P.Telephone = ?
WHERE C.CustomerID = ?;

SELECT P.PersonID, P.LastName, P.FirstName, P.Telephone, C.CustomerID, C.EmailAddress
FROM PERSON P JOIN CUSTOMER C ON C.PersonID = P.PersonID
WHERE C.CustomerID = ?
ORDER BY C.CustomerID;

notes: The PERSON row is found through CUSTOMER, so independently supplied person and customer identifiers cannot update two different people. Both updates run in one transaction. Other editable contact columns can be included in the same pattern.

title: Add employee
definition: Create a personal record and an employment record, including the employee role.

parameters.name: PersonID
parameters.description: Unused identifier for the new PERSON row.

parameters.name: ZipCode
parameters.description: Postal code, stored as text to preserve leading zeros.

parameters.name: HourlyRate
parameters.description: Nonnegative hourly rate in the team schema.

statements.sql:
INSERT INTO PERSON (PersonID, LastName, FirstName, Address, City, State, ZipCode, Telephone)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?);

INSERT INTO EMPLOYEE (SocialSecurityNumber, PersonID, StartDate, HourlyRate, EmployeeType)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?);

SELECT E.SocialSecurityNumber, P.PersonID, P.FirstName, P.LastName, P.Address, P.City,
       P.State, P.ZipCode, P.Telephone, E.StartDate, E.HourlyRate, E.EmployeeType
FROM EMPLOYEE E JOIN PERSON P ON P.PersonID = E.PersonID
WHERE E.SocialSecurityNumber = ?
ORDER BY E.SocialSecurityNumber;

notes: The two inserts are atomic and bind the same PersonID. The test uses an unused identifier and is rolled back before other tests reuse PersonID 7. Only a manager may execute this transaction.

title: Edit employee hourly rate
definition: Change the hourly rate of an existing employee.

statements.sql:
SELECT E.SocialSecurityNumber, P.FirstName, P.LastName, E.StartDate, E.HourlyRate, E.EmployeeType
FROM EMPLOYEE E JOIN PERSON P ON P.PersonID = E.PersonID
WHERE E.SocialSecurityNumber = ?
ORDER BY E.SocialSecurityNumber;

notes: This demonstrates an employee-information edit. Personal-field updates should identify PERSON through the EMPLOYEE join, using the same employee identifier. Changing a representative into a manager requires a separate policy for existing HANDLEDBY history. Hourly rates are manager-only information.

title: Add movie
definition: Add a new movie to the catalog with its total number of copies.

parameters.name: NumberOfCopies
parameters.description: Nonnegative total inventory, not the count currently available.

statements.sql:
INSERT INTO MOVIE (MovieID, MovieName, MovieType, DistributionFee, NumberOfCopies, Rating)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?);

SELECT MovieID, MovieName, MovieType, DistributionFee, NumberOfCopies, Rating
FROM MOVIE
WHERE MovieID = ?
ORDER BY MovieID;

notes: Availability is calculated from total copies minus unreturned rentals. Adding a movie does not create actor associations; those are inserted separately.

title: Delete movie
definition: Delete a catalog movie that has no rental history.

parameters.name: MovieID
parameters.description: Identifier of the movie to delete.

statements.sql:
DELETE FROM MOVIE
WHERE MovieID = ?;

SELECT MovieID, MovieName, MovieType, DistributionFee, NumberOfCopies, Rating
FROM MOVIE
WHERE MovieID = ?
ORDER BY MovieID;

notes: ORDER_MOVIE has a restrictive foreign key to MOVIE, so a movie with rental history cannot be deleted. Do not delete rental history to bypass that restriction. Existing FEATURES, QUEUES, and RATES references follow their declared cascade rules. The test first inserts an unused temporary movie; setup and deletion are rolled back together.

setup.sql:
INSERT INTO MOVIE (MovieID, MovieName, MovieType, DistributionFee, NumberOfCopies, Rating)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?);

title: Add actor
definition: Add an actor to the catalog. This is an additional operation retained from the team draft.

parameters.name: Gender
parameters.description: M or F, matching the given schema and demo data.

statements.sql:
INSERT INTO ACTOR (ActorID, ActorName, Gender, Age, Rating)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?);

SELECT ActorID, ActorName, Gender, Age, Rating
FROM ACTOR
WHERE ActorID = ?
ORDER BY ActorID;

notes: This is supplementary catalog maintenance. An actor is associated with a movie using FEATURES.

title: Edit actor
definition: Update an actor age and popularity rating.

statements.sql:
SELECT ActorID, ActorName, Gender, Age, Rating
FROM ACTOR
WHERE ActorID = ?
ORDER BY ActorID;

notes: Supplementary catalog maintenance. The actor identifier stays unchanged.

title: Delete actor
definition: Delete an actor from the catalog.

parameters.name: ActorID
parameters.description: Identifier of the actor to delete.

statements.sql:
DELETE FROM ACTOR
WHERE ActorID = ?;

SELECT ActorID, ActorName, Gender, Age, Rating
FROM ACTOR
WHERE ActorID = ?
ORDER BY ActorID;

notes: FEATURES associations cascade when an actor is deleted. Movie rows and rental rows are not deleted. The test creates an unused temporary actor, then deletes that actor inside the same rollback-isolated test.

setup.sql:
INSERT INTO ACTOR (ActorID, ActorName, Gender, Age, Rating)
VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?);

title: Add actor to movie
definition: Associate an existing actor with an existing movie.

statements.sql:
INSERT INTO FEATURES (MovieID, ActorID)
VALUES (?, ?);

SELECT F.MovieID, M.MovieName, F.ActorID, A.ActorName
FROM FEATURES F
JOIN MOVIE M ON M.MovieID = F.MovieID
JOIN ACTOR A ON A.ActorID = F.ActorID
WHERE F.MovieID = ?
ORDER BY F.MovieID, F.ActorID;

notes: The composite primary key prevents duplicate associations. Both foreign keys must reference existing rows. This is a deliberate test change, not a correction to the official demo data.

title: Remove actor from movie
definition: Remove one cast association without deleting the movie or actor.

parameters.name: ActorID
parameters.description: Actor identifier in the association to remove.

statements.sql:
DELETE FROM FEATURES
WHERE MovieID = ? AND ActorID = ?;

SELECT F.MovieID, M.MovieName, F.ActorID, A.ActorName
FROM FEATURES F
JOIN MOVIE M ON M.MovieID = F.MovieID
JOIN ACTOR A ON A.ActorID = F.ActorID
WHERE F.MovieID = ?
ORDER BY F.MovieID, F.ActorID;

notes: Only the specified FEATURES row is deleted. The actor, movie, and rental history remain. The test rollback restores the demo association.

title: Monthly subscription income estimate
definition: Estimate subscription income for a selected calendar month using the current account records and the project's fixed monthly plan fees.

parameters.name: MonthStart
parameters.description: First day of the requested month; the application must validate this requirement.

sql:
WITH report_parameters AS (
    SELECT CAST(? AS DATE) AS MonthStart
)
SELECT rp.MonthStart AS ReportMonth,
       COUNT(a.AccountNumber) AS AssumedActiveSubscriptions,
       CAST(COALESCE(SUM(
           CASE a.AccountType
               WHEN 'Lim' THEN 10.00
               WHEN 'Unlim1' THEN 15.00
               WHEN 'Unlim2' THEN 20.00
               WHEN 'Unlim3' THEN 25.00
               ELSE 0.00
           END
       ), 0.00) AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS EstimatedMonthlyIncome
FROM report_parameters rp
LEFT JOIN ACCOUNT a
    ON a.AccountCreationDate < DATE_ADD(rp.MonthStart, INTERVAL 1 MONTH)
GROUP BY rp.MonthStart;
notes: Estimate only: assumes every retained account remains active from its creation onward, its current plan applied in the report month, and the full monthly fee is charged for any month in which the account exists, without proration. ACCOUNT contains no cancellation/status history, plan-change history, invoices, or payments; exact historical active-subscription income cannot be reconstructed. DistributionFee is an expense and is not rental/subscription income. All four prices come from the project requirements.

title: Comprehensive movie listing
definition: List every catalog movie, including unavailable movies and movies without cast entries, together with current circulation counts and its actors.
sql:
SELECT v.MovieID, v.MovieName, v.MovieType, v.DistributionFee,
       v.NumberOfCopies, v.Rating, v.CopiesOut, v.AvailableCopies,
       GROUP_CONCAT(a.ActorName ORDER BY a.ActorName, a.ActorID SEPARATOR ', ') AS Actors
FROM V_MOVIE_AVAILABILITY v
LEFT JOIN FEATURES f ON f.MovieID = v.MovieID
LEFT JOIN ACTOR a ON a.ActorID = f.ActorID
GROUP BY v.MovieID, v.MovieName, v.MovieType, v.DistributionFee,
         v.NumberOfCopies, v.Rating, v.CopiesOut, v.AvailableCopies
ORDER BY v.MovieID;
notes: V_MOVIE_AVAILABILITY must contain one row per movie and count only orders with ReturnDateTime IS NULL as CopiesOut; AvailableCopies is NumberOfCopies minus CopiesOut. LEFT JOIN retains movies with no FEATURES rows; Actors is NULL for such movies. This manager catalog report deliberately includes movies with zero available copies. GROUP_CONCAT is suitable for the demo cast sizes; increase its session limit for a larger production catalog if necessary.

title: Rental history by movie name
definition: List current and returned rentals for every movie matching the supplied title.

parameters.name: MovieName
parameters.description: Exact movie title, compared using the database collation.

sql:
SELECT o.OrderID, m.MovieID, m.MovieName, m.MovieType,
       ac.AccountNumber, ac.CustomerID,
       o.OrderDateTime, o.ReturnDateTime
FROM MOVIE m
JOIN ORDER_MOVIE om ON om.MovieID = m.MovieID
JOIN ORDERR o ON o.OrderID = om.OrderID
JOIN PLACES pl ON pl.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN ACCOUNT ac ON ac.AccountNumber = pl.AccountNumber
WHERE m.MovieName = ?
ORDER BY o.OrderDateTime, o.OrderID;
notes: MovieName is not declared unique; MovieID is included so separate titles with identical names remain distinguishable. The manager sees all matching customers' rentals, including currently outstanding rentals.

title: Rental history by movie type
definition: List current and returned rentals for movies of a selected type.

parameters.name: MovieType
parameters.description: One of Comedy, Drama, Action, or Foreign.

sql:
SELECT o.OrderID, m.MovieID, m.MovieName, m.MovieType,
       ac.AccountNumber, ac.CustomerID,
       o.OrderDateTime, o.ReturnDateTime
FROM MOVIE m
JOIN ORDER_MOVIE om ON om.MovieID = m.MovieID
JOIN ORDERR o ON o.OrderID = om.OrderID
JOIN PLACES pl ON pl.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN ACCOUNT ac ON ac.AccountNumber = pl.AccountNumber
WHERE m.MovieType = ?
ORDER BY o.OrderDateTime, o.OrderID;
notes: This rental-history report does not filter availability: both returned and currently held orders are relevant.

title: Rental history by customer name
definition: List current and returned rentals across all accounts of customers matching the supplied first and last names.
sql:
SELECT c.CustomerID, p.FirstName, p.LastName,
       ac.AccountNumber, o.OrderID, m.MovieID, m.MovieName,
       o.OrderDateTime, o.ReturnDateTime
FROM PERSON p
JOIN CUSTOMER c ON c.PersonID = p.PersonID
JOIN ACCOUNT ac ON ac.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
JOIN PLACES pl ON pl.AccountNumber = ac.AccountNumber
JOIN ORDERR o ON o.OrderID = pl.OrderID
JOIN ORDER_MOVIE om ON om.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN MOVIE m ON m.MovieID = om.MovieID
WHERE p.FirstName = ? AND p.LastName = ?
ORDER BY c.CustomerID, o.OrderDateTime, o.OrderID;
notes: Names are not unique. This report returns every matching customer and includes CustomerID to distinguish them. Counts and history span all of each customer's accounts.

title: Customer representatives who handled the most rentals
definition: Find all customer representatives tied for the largest positive number of handled rental orders.
sql:
WITH representative_counts AS (
    SELECT e.SocialSecurityNumber, p.FirstName, p.LastName,
           COUNT(om.OrderID) AS OrdersHandled
    FROM EMPLOYEE e
    JOIN PERSON p ON p.PersonID = e.PersonID
    LEFT JOIN HANDLEDBY h ON h.SocialSecurityNumber = e.SocialSecurityNumber
    LEFT JOIN ORDERR o ON o.OrderID = h.OrderID
    LEFT JOIN ORDER_MOVIE om ON om.OrderID = o.OrderID
    WHERE e.EmployeeType = 'CustomerRepresentative'
    GROUP BY e.SocialSecurityNumber, p.FirstName, p.LastName
)
SELECT SocialSecurityNumber, FirstName, LastName, OrdersHandled
FROM representative_counts
WHERE OrdersHandled > 0
  AND OrdersHandled = (SELECT MAX(OrdersHandled) FROM representative_counts)
ORDER BY SocialSecurityNumber;
notes: Returns every first-place tie, without LIMIT 1. If no customer representative has handled any rental, the result is empty. Counted orders must have an ORDER_MOVIE record. The source demo omits all HANDLEDBY records; any demo fixture assigning the four orders to the sole representative must be documented as an added assumption, not original data.

title: Most active customers, including all first-place ties
definition: Find all customers tied for the largest positive number of rental orders across their accounts.
sql:
WITH rental_counts AS (
    SELECT ac.CustomerID, COUNT(om.OrderID) AS TotalRentals
    FROM ACCOUNT ac
    JOIN PLACES pl ON pl.AccountNumber = ac.AccountNumber
    JOIN ORDERR o ON o.OrderID = pl.OrderID
    JOIN ORDER_MOVIE om ON om.OrderID = o.OrderID
    GROUP BY ac.CustomerID
)
SELECT c.CustomerID, p.FirstName, p.LastName, rc.TotalRentals
FROM rental_counts rc
JOIN CUSTOMER c ON c.CustomerID = rc.CustomerID
JOIN PERSON p ON p.PersonID = c.PersonID
WHERE rc.TotalRentals > 0
  AND rc.TotalRentals = (SELECT MAX(TotalRentals) FROM rental_counts)
ORDER BY c.CustomerID;
notes: All first-place ties are retained. Each rental order counts once, including repeat rentals of a title and currently held movies. This measures activity from orders rather than the seed CUSTOMER.Rating. Customers with no rentals are not most active; an entirely unrented database returns no rows.

title: Most actively rented movies / customer best-seller list
definition: Rank all catalog movies by all-time rental count, with equal counts receiving the same rank.
sql:
WITH movie_counts AS (
    SELECT m.MovieID, m.MovieName, m.MovieType,
           COUNT(o.OrderID) AS RentalCount
    FROM MOVIE m
    LEFT JOIN ORDER_MOVIE om ON om.MovieID = m.MovieID
    LEFT JOIN ORDERR o ON o.OrderID = om.OrderID
    GROUP BY m.MovieID, m.MovieName, m.MovieType
)
SELECT MovieID, MovieName, MovieType, RentalCount,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY RentalCount DESC) AS PopularityRank
FROM movie_counts
ORDER BY RentalCount DESC, MovieID;
notes: The same query serves the manager's most-actively-rented-movies report and the customer's best-seller list. Counts include current and past rentals and retain never-rented movies with zero. DENSE_RANK preserves tied popularity while MovieID makes output order deterministic. The best-seller list is not an availability search and may include unavailable movies.

title: Customer mailing list
definition: List customers' names, mailing addresses, and email addresses, including customers without an account.
sql:
SELECT c.CustomerID, p.FirstName, p.LastName,
       p.Address, p.City, p.State, p.ZipCode, c.EmailAddress
FROM CUSTOMER c
JOIN PERSON p ON p.PersonID = c.PersonID
ORDER BY p.LastName, p.FirstName, c.CustomerID;
notes: This is a staff-only customer report. No credit card data is selected, and no ACCOUNT join excludes customers who have not yet opened an account.

title: Nearest-neighbor movie suggestions
definition: Recommend unrented movies from customers with the greatest positive overlap in previously rented distinct movie titles.

parameters.name: TargetCustomerID
parameters.description: For customer self-service, bind the authenticated session's CustomerID. A role-authorized representative may select the customer to assist.

sql:
WITH target_customer AS (
    SELECT CustomerID
    FROM CUSTOMER
    WHERE CustomerID = ?
),
rental_history AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ac.CustomerID, om.MovieID
    FROM ACCOUNT ac
    JOIN PLACES pl ON pl.AccountNumber = ac.AccountNumber
    JOIN ORDERR o ON o.OrderID = pl.OrderID
    JOIN ORDER_MOVIE om ON om.OrderID = o.OrderID
),
overlap_scores AS (
    SELECT other.CustomerID, COUNT(*) AS SharedTitles
    FROM target_customer target
    JOIN rental_history own ON own.CustomerID = target.CustomerID
    JOIN rental_history other
      ON other.MovieID = own.MovieID
     AND other.CustomerID <> target.CustomerID
    GROUP BY other.CustomerID
),
nearest_neighbors AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, SharedTitles
    FROM overlap_scores
    WHERE SharedTitles = (SELECT MAX(SharedTitles) FROM overlap_scores)
)
SELECT m.MovieID, m.MovieName, m.MovieType,
       COUNT(DISTINCT neighbor.CustomerID) AS RecommendingNeighbors,
       MAX(neighbor.SharedTitles) AS NearestNeighborSharedTitles
FROM nearest_neighbors neighbor
JOIN rental_history candidate ON candidate.CustomerID = neighbor.CustomerID
JOIN MOVIE m ON m.MovieID = candidate.MovieID
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM rental_history prior_rental
    JOIN target_customer target ON target.CustomerID = prior_rental.CustomerID
    WHERE prior_rental.MovieID = m.MovieID
)
GROUP BY m.MovieID, m.MovieName, m.MovieType
ORDER BY RecommendingNeighbors DESC, m.MovieID;
notes: One query is reused for representative-assisted and customer self-service suggestions. Customer calls must bind TargetCustomerID from the trusted session; the server must authorize representatives before permitting a different target. Similarity is the number of shared distinct rented titles, not Jaccard similarity or ratings. All customers tied for the largest positive overlap are nearest neighbors. Histories combine all accounts of each customer, exclude the target customer from neighbors, and exclude all of the target's previously rented titles. Repeat rentals do not inflate similarity. No history, no overlapping neighbor, or no unseen neighbor titles yields an empty result. RATES is not required. Suggestions may be queued even when unavailable; checkout separately enforces availability.

title: Customer's currently held movies
definition: List unreturned rentals for an account owned by the authenticated customer.

parameters.name: AuthenticatedCustomerID
parameters.description: Customer ID obtained from the trusted authenticated session, never from editable form data.

sql:
SELECT m.MovieID, m.MovieName, m.MovieType,
       o.OrderID, o.OrderDateTime
FROM ACCOUNT ac
JOIN PLACES pl ON pl.AccountNumber = ac.AccountNumber
JOIN ORDERR o ON o.OrderID = pl.OrderID
JOIN ORDER_MOVIE om ON om.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN MOVIE m ON m.MovieID = om.MovieID
WHERE ac.AccountNumber = ?
  AND ac.CustomerID = ?
  AND o.ReturnDateTime IS NULL
ORDER BY o.OrderDateTime, o.OrderID;
notes: The server must obtain AuthenticatedCustomerID from the authenticated session and authorize the customer role before executing this statement. A mismatched account/customer pair returns no rows. The current schema does not itself model login identities or database role privileges.

title: Customer's movie queue
definition: List the authenticated customer's selected account queue in its requested viewing order.

parameters.name: AuthenticatedCustomerID
parameters.description: Customer ID obtained from the trusted authenticated session, never from editable form data.

sql:
SELECT q.QueuePosition, m.MovieID, m.MovieName, m.MovieType
FROM ACCOUNT ac
JOIN QUEUES q ON q.AccountNumber = ac.AccountNumber
JOIN MOVIE m ON m.MovieID = q.MovieID
WHERE ac.AccountNumber = ?
  AND ac.CustomerID = ?
ORDER BY q.QueuePosition;
notes: The server must obtain AuthenticatedCustomerID from the authenticated session and authorize the customer role before executing this statement. A mismatched account/customer pair returns no rows. The current schema does not itself model login identities or database role privileges. The queue includes unavailable movies; it records viewing preferences rather than a promise of immediate checkout.

title: Customer's account settings
definition: Display the authenticated customer's selected account, subscription fee, contact details, and masked payment-card number.

parameters.name: AuthenticatedCustomerID
parameters.description: Customer ID obtained from the trusted authenticated session, never from editable form data.

sql:
SELECT ac.AccountNumber, ac.CustomerID, ac.AccountType, ac.AccountCreationDate,
       CASE ac.AccountType
           WHEN 'Lim' THEN 10.00
           WHEN 'Unlim1' THEN 15.00
           WHEN 'Unlim2' THEN 20.00
           WHEN 'Unlim3' THEN 25.00
       END AS MonthlyFee,
       p.FirstName, p.LastName, p.Address, p.City, p.State,
       p.ZipCode, p.Telephone, c.EmailAddress,
       CONCAT('****-****-****-', RIGHT(c.CreditCardNumber, 4)) AS MaskedCreditCardNumber
FROM ACCOUNT ac
JOIN CUSTOMER c ON c.CustomerID = ac.CustomerID
JOIN PERSON p ON p.PersonID = c.PersonID
WHERE ac.AccountNumber = ?
  AND ac.CustomerID = ?;
notes: The server must obtain AuthenticatedCustomerID from the authenticated session and authorize the customer role before executing this statement. A mismatched account/customer pair returns no rows. The current schema does not itself model login identities or database role privileges. Only the last four card digits are displayed. The demo schema retains a full card-number field; this query does not expose that full value.

title: Customer's current and past order history
definition: List all rental orders for an account owned by the authenticated customer, explicitly marking currently held and returned movies.

parameters.name: AuthenticatedCustomerID
parameters.description: Customer ID obtained from the trusted authenticated session, never from editable form data.

sql:
SELECT o.OrderID, o.OrderDateTime, o.ReturnDateTime,
       m.MovieID, m.MovieName, m.MovieType,
       CASE WHEN o.ReturnDateTime IS NULL THEN 'Currently held' ELSE 'Returned' END AS RentalStatus
FROM ACCOUNT ac
JOIN PLACES pl ON pl.AccountNumber = ac.AccountNumber
JOIN ORDERR o ON o.OrderID = pl.OrderID
JOIN ORDER_MOVIE om ON om.OrderID = o.OrderID
JOIN MOVIE m ON m.MovieID = om.MovieID
WHERE ac.AccountNumber = ?
  AND ac.CustomerID = ?
ORDER BY o.OrderDateTime, o.OrderID;
notes: The server must obtain AuthenticatedCustomerID from the authenticated session and authorize the customer role before executing this statement. A mismatched account/customer pair returns no rows. The current schema does not itself model login identities or database role privileges.

title: Available movies by type
definition: Find movies of a selected type with at least one copy currently available.

parameters.name: MovieType
parameters.description: One of Comedy, Drama, Action, or Foreign.

sql:
SELECT MovieID, MovieName, MovieType, Rating, AvailableCopies
FROM V_MOVIE_AVAILABILITY
WHERE MovieType = ?
  AND AvailableCopies > 0
ORDER BY MovieName, MovieID;
notes: Availability is derived from outstanding rentals, not merely NumberOfCopies > 0. Availability can change after this read; the order transaction must recheck inventory under its checkout locking protocol.

title: Available movies by one literal title keyword
definition: Find available movies whose title contains the supplied literal keyword.

parameters.name: Keyword
parameters.description: Nonempty literal title substring; the application trims and rejects blank input.

sql:
SELECT MovieID, MovieName, MovieType, Rating, AvailableCopies
FROM V_MOVIE_AVAILABILITY
WHERE AvailableCopies > 0
  AND LOCATE(?, MovieName) > 0
ORDER BY MovieName, MovieID;
notes: LOCATE treats percent and underscore characters literally; it does not interpret SQL LIKE wildcard syntax. Case/accent matching follows the configured string collation. A query parameter is bound as data.

title: Available movies containing all requested title keywords
definition: Find available movies whose title contains both supplied literal keywords, in any order.
sql:
SELECT MovieID, MovieName, MovieType, Rating, AvailableCopies
FROM V_MOVIE_AVAILABILITY
WHERE AvailableCopies > 0
  AND LOCATE(?, MovieName) > 0
  AND LOCATE(?, MovieName) > 0
ORDER BY MovieName, MovieID;
notes: The keyword-set semantics are ALL, not ANY. This fixed two-keyword query satisfies the demonstrated set search; additional keywords use additional bound LOCATE predicates. Trim input and reject blank or NULL keywords. Repeating a keyword does not require it to appear twice.

title: Available movies starring a selected actor
definition: Find available movies featuring the selected actor ID.

parameters.name: ActorID
parameters.description: ID of the actor selected by name in the interface; actor names are not declared unique.

sql:
SELECT v.MovieID, v.MovieName, v.MovieType, v.Rating, v.AvailableCopies
FROM V_MOVIE_AVAILABILITY v
WHERE v.AvailableCopies > 0
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM FEATURES f
      WHERE f.MovieID = v.MovieID AND f.ActorID = ?
  )
ORDER BY v.MovieName, v.MovieID;
notes: Use the ACTOR primary key for an unambiguous actor selection. FEATURES is keyed by (MovieID, ActorID), and EXISTS does not duplicate movie rows. The test ActorID 1 is Al Pacino in the team's supplied data.

title: Available movies starring all selected actors
definition: Find available movies featuring both selected actor IDs.
sql:
SELECT v.MovieID, v.MovieName, v.MovieType, v.Rating, v.AvailableCopies
FROM V_MOVIE_AVAILABILITY v
WHERE v.AvailableCopies > 0
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM FEATURES f1
      WHERE f1.MovieID = v.MovieID AND f1.ActorID = ?
  )
  AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM FEATURES f2
      WHERE f2.MovieID = v.MovieID AND f2.ActorID = ?
  )
ORDER BY v.MovieName, v.MovieID;
notes: The actor-group semantics are ALL. Separate EXISTS predicates also handle duplicate actor selections correctly: selecting the same actor twice is equivalent to selecting that actor once. Additional selected actor IDs use additional bound EXISTS predicates. The team's data associates actor 1 Al Pacino and actor 2 Tim Robbins with movie 1; this preserves the supplied fictional/demo cast assignments.

title: Employee information visible to customer representatives
definition: List employee identification, contact, start-date, and role information while excluding hourly pay.
sql:
SELECT e.SocialSecurityNumber, e.PersonID,
       p.FirstName, p.LastName, p.Address, p.City, p.State,
       p.ZipCode, p.Telephone, e.StartDate, e.EmployeeType
FROM EMPLOYEE e
JOIN PERSON p ON p.PersonID = e.PersonID
ORDER BY p.LastName, p.FirstName, e.SocialSecurityNumber;
notes: HourlyRate is intentionally absent, as required by the project. Authorize the customer-representative role server-side; customers must not receive employee information. This safe projection is not a substitute for controlled database/API access to the EMPLOYEE base table.

title: Record a rental / customer places an order
definition: Create one rental and all three mandatory associations atomically, while enforcing copies, plan limits, representative role, ownership, and queue removal.

parameters.name: AuthenticatedCustomerID
parameters.description: Trusted customer identity from the application session, not a user-editable form field.

parameters.name: RentalDateTime
parameters.description: Rental time; tests use fixed demo-era dates.

statements.sql: CALL rent_movie(?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?);

SELECT o.OrderID, p.AccountNumber, om.MovieID, h.SocialSecurityNumber, o.OrderDateTime, o.ReturnDateTime FROM ORDERR o JOIN PLACES p USING (OrderID) JOIN ORDER_MOVIE om USING (OrderID) JOIN HANDLEDBY h USING (OrderID) WHERE o.OrderID = ?;
SELECT * FROM QUEUES WHERE AccountNumber = ? ORDER BY QueuePosition;

notes: Full SQL is rent_movie in 02_transaction_procedures.sql. READ COMMITTED plus account/movie row locks serialize cooperating rental writers. All application rental writes must use this path; raw direct table writes bypass it. A duplicate OrderID fails and rolls back. Calendar months determine the limited-plan quota.

title: Return a movie and offer the next available queued movie
definition: Mark the current rental returned and attempt one next-available queue fulfillment in the same transaction. A quota/full account or no available queue item leaves fulfillment waiting.

parameters.name: AuthenticatedCustomerID
parameters.description: Trusted customer identity from the application session, not a user-editable form field.

parameters.name: NewOrderID
parameters.description: Unused ID for possible next rental.

statements.sql: CALL return_movie(?, ?, ?, ?);
CALL fulfill_next(?, ?, ?, ?, ?);
SELECT * FROM ORDERR WHERE OrderID IN (3, 5) ORDER BY OrderID;

SELECT o.OrderID, p.AccountNumber, om.MovieID, h.SocialSecurityNumber, o.OrderDateTime, o.ReturnDateTime FROM ORDERR o JOIN PLACES p USING (OrderID) JOIN ORDER_MOVIE om USING (OrderID) JOIN HANDLEDBY h USING (OrderID) WHERE o.OrderID = ?;
SELECT * FROM QUEUES WHERE AccountNumber = 1 ORDER BY QueuePosition;

notes: The original order and its customer/movie/representative links remain intact. If fulfillment raises an actual SQL error, both steps roll back. A routine waiting result is not an error and the return can commit. Deadlock/lock-timeout errors require the application to retry the entire transaction.

title: Add a movie to the queue
definition: Append a movie once at the end of the account queue.

parameters.name: AuthenticatedCustomerID
parameters.description: Trusted customer identity from the application session, not a user-editable form field.

statements.sql: CALL queue_add(?, ?, ?);
SELECT * FROM QUEUES WHERE AccountNumber = ? ORDER BY QueuePosition;

notes: Queue policy: each account queues each title at most once; positions remain consecutive through the supplied queue operations. Unavailable movies may be queued.

title: Remove a queued movie
definition: Remove one position and close the gap.

parameters.name: AuthenticatedCustomerID
parameters.description: Trusted customer identity from the application session, not a user-editable form field.

statements.sql: CALL queue_remove(?, ?, ?);
SELECT * FROM QUEUES WHERE AccountNumber = ? ORDER BY QueuePosition;

title: Reorder the movie queue
definition: Move a queued movie to another position and shift the intervening entries.

parameters.name: AuthenticatedCustomerID
parameters.description: Trusted customer identity from the application session, not a user-editable form field.

statements.sql: CALL queue_move(?, ?, ?, ?);
SELECT * FROM QUEUES WHERE AccountNumber = ? ORDER BY QueuePosition;

notes: Uses a temporary positive position and ordered updates to avoid transient duplicate primary keys.

title: Rate a previously rented movie
definition: Insert a rating or replace the account's existing rating after checking rental history and ownership.

parameters.name: AuthenticatedCustomerID
parameters.description: Trusted customer identity from the application session, not a user-editable form field.

statements.sql: CALL rate_movie(?, ?, ?, ?);
SELECT * FROM RATES WHERE AccountNumber = ? AND MovieID = ?;

notes: RATES stores the individual customer rating. MOVIE.Rating remains the supplied catalog popularity score; it is not silently overwritten with the first user rating.

title: Update an existing movie rating

parameters.name: AuthenticatedCustomerID

statements.sql: CALL rate_movie(?, ?, ?, ?);

title: Delete an unreferenced customer
definition: Delete a customer with no rental history, and delete the person only if they are not also an employee.

parameters.name: CustomerID
parameters.description: Existing customer with no protected rental history.

statements.sql: CALL delete_customer(?);
SELECT * FROM CUSTOMER WHERE CustomerID = ?;
SELECT * FROM PERSON WHERE PersonID = ?;

notes: Deletion of a customer with rental history is rejected by the preserved foreign keys. This prevents orphaned past/current orders. Deactivation and historical subscription accounting would require a separate agreed schema extension.

title: Delete an unreferenced employee
definition: Delete an employee with no handled rentals; retain PERSON if also a customer.

statements.sql: CALL delete_employee(?);
SELECT * FROM EMPLOYEE WHERE SocialSecurityNumber = ?;
SELECT * FROM PERSON WHERE PersonID = ?;

notes: The demo manager has no handled rentals. Production must separately prevent removal of the last login-capable manager; no login lifecycle is modeled in this schema.

statements.sql: INSERT INTO ACCOUNT (AccountNumber, CustomerID, AccountType, AccountCreationDate) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?);
